title: Effects of double-dose algebra on college persistence and degree attainment
authors: Takako Nomi, Stephen W. Raudenbush, and Julia S. Smith
finding: Chicago's double-dose algebra policy is a distinct extended-instruction case with evidence on high-school and postsecondary progression for students assigned around a prior-score cutoff.
caveat: The design is strongest near the policy cutoff, and effects depend on a specific district policy, course grouping, and implementation period.

title: Principal Pipelines: A Feasible, Affordable, and Effective Way for Districts to Improve Schools
finding: Across participating districts, pipeline schools with newly placed principals outperformed matched comparison schools after sustained implementation, alongside improved principal retention.
caveat: The evaluation estimates a coherent district leadership package, not the isolated effect of one hiring, preparation, evaluation, or support component.

title: Effects of Dual-Language Immersion Programs on Student Achievement: Evidence from Lottery Data
finding: Lottery evidence reviewed by the What Works Clearinghouse supports potentially positive English-literacy effects for dual-language programs, with uncertain results in some other subjects.
caveat: Program model, language pair, student composition, duration, and whether biliteracy is counted as an outcome all affect interpretation.

title: Getting students on track for graduation: Impacts of the Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System after one year
finding: In 73 randomly assigned high schools, EWIMS reduced chronic absence and course failure in year one but did not produce a detectable improvement in on-track credit accumulation.
caveat: Implementation of the full process was difficult, and the first-year study does not establish an effect on graduation.

title: The Causal Effects of Cultural Relevance: Evidence from an Ethnic Studies Curriculum
authors: Thomas S. Dee and Emily K. Penner
finding: A San Francisco pilot assigned around an eighth-grade GPA threshold produced large improvements in ninth-grade attendance, GPA, and credits earned for students near the cutoff.
caveat: This is a high-fidelity, place-specific pilot; it should not be treated as evidence that every ethnic studies implementation will have the same effect.

title: Impacts of Comprehensive Teacher Induction: Final Results from a Randomized Controlled Study
finding: The national randomized evaluation found more support for treated beginning teachers but no consistent effect on retention, classroom practice, or student achievement for one-year induction.
caveat: A later positive result for a two-year subset requires narrower interpretation and does not overturn the broadly null first- and second-year findings.

title: Evaluation of the National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Program
finding: A ten-site random-assignment evaluation found that participants were more likely to earn a diploma or GED, earn college credits, and work; earnings were higher after three years.
caveat: The intensive residential alternative program serves a selected population of young people who are disconnected from conventional school pathways.

title: The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Final Report: The Impact of Supplemental Literacy Courses for Struggling Ninth Graders
authors: Marie-Andree Somers, William Corrin, Susan Sepanik, and colleagues
finding: Across 34 high schools, supplemental literacy courses improved ninth-grade reading comprehension, core academic performance, and credit accumulation, but effects did not persist after the program year.
caveat: The combined result masks differences between Reading Apprenticeship Academic Literacy and Xtreme Reading, and most students remained far below grade level.

title: When Schools Stay Open Late: The National Evaluation of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Program
finding: The federal after-school evaluation found few academic effects, improved perceived safety for elementary participants, and mixed developmental and behavior results.
caveat: Attendance intensity was limited, and the study evaluates the program model and period studied rather than every modern after-school design.

title: The Effect of Free School Meals on Household Food Purchases: Evidence from the Community Eligibility Provision
authors: Michelle M. Marcus and Katherine G. Yewell
finding: Universal free meals through Community Eligibility Provision exposure reduced household food purchases and was associated with improved dietary quality and lower food insecurity for lower-income households.
caveat: This evidence concerns household and food-security outcomes; it does not by itself establish academic effects for students.

title: Talent Development High Schools
finding: The reviewed evidence did not show a discernible effect on progressing in school, despite a real large-high-school restructuring model aimed at attendance, achievement, and dropout prevention.
caveat: The review covers a limited evidence base and should not be read as a verdict on every ninth-grade academy or small-learning-community implementation.

title: The Impressive Effects of Tutoring on PreK-12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
authors: Andre Nickow, Philip Oreopoulos, and Vincent Quan
finding: Across experimental tutoring studies, tutoring produced meaningful average learning gains, with larger effects when programs were delivered during the school day, frequently, and by trained adults or near peers.
caveat: The pooled estimate spans different grades, subjects, delivery models, and study settings; it does not establish that every tutoring implementation achieves the average effect.

title: Examining the Effects of Schoolwide Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports on Student Outcomes
authors: Catherine P. Bradshaw, Mary M. Mitchell, and Philip J. Leaf
finding: In a five-year randomized trial across 37 elementary schools, trained schools implemented PBIS with high fidelity and had lower suspensions and office discipline referrals.
caveat: The study's clearest impacts were behavioral and disciplinary; it should not be read as direct proof of broad academic gains in every PBIS implementation.

title: Early College, Continued Success: Longer-Term Impact of Early College High Schools
authors: Mengli Song, Kristina Zeiser, Drew Atchison, and Iliana Brodziak de los Reyes
finding: Longer-term follow-up of early college admissions found sustained postsecondary benefits, including college enrollment and credential outcomes, for students offered access through oversubscribed schools.
caveat: The design estimates effects for applicants to participating early colleges and does not automatically generalize to every dual-enrollment or early-college model.

title: Head Start Impact Study: Final Report
authors: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families
finding: The national randomized study found initial improvements in selected preschool outcomes, while many measured differences had narrowed by the end of kindergarten or first grade.
caveat: Children assigned to the control group often used other early-childhood services, and the report's measured early-test convergence does not settle possible longer-run or non-test effects.

title: The Impact of Restorative Practices on Student Outcomes in Pittsburgh Public Schools
finding: A randomized evaluation of Pittsburgh's whole-school restorative-practices program found implementation and climate changes but did not find the expected broad reductions in suspension or improvement in academic outcomes during the study period.
caveat: This evaluates a particular district rollout with uneven implementation; it does not establish that every restorative practice or narrower discipline intervention has the same effects.

title: School Finance Reform and the Distribution of Student Achievement
authors: Julien Lafortune, Jesse Rothstein, and Diane Whitmore Schanzenbach
finding: Difference-in-differences evidence links post-1990 finance reforms to gains in district test scores, with larger gains for lower-income districts and narrower achievement gaps in many reform states.
caveat: Effects vary with the reform's size and design, and a policy-induced association cannot identify the exact school-level uses of additional funding that produced the gains.

title: Case Studies of Schools Receiving School Improvement Grants: Final Report
authors: Kerstin Carlson Le Floch and colleagues
finding: Case studies of 25 SIG schools document the implementation choices, capacity constraints, and sustainability challenges that accompanied the federal turnaround grants.
caveat: The purposive case-study design supplies implementation context but does not estimate a causal effect on student outcomes.

title: Evaluation of the Teacher Incentive Fund: Final Report on Implementation and Impacts of Pay-for-Performance Across Four Years
finding: The randomized Teacher Incentive Fund evaluation found a positive fourth-year average achievement impact alongside substantial implementation and sustainability variation across grantees.
caveat: The estimate is for a bundled federal pay-for-performance model, not for every merit-pay plan or for bonuses in isolation.

title: An Evaluation of California Partnership Academies: Charting the Path from High School to Postsecondary Enrollment
authors: Susan Sepanik, Kenny Nguyen, and Bryce Marshall
finding: A newer randomized evaluation of the career-academy model found no overall effect on college readiness or first-year postsecondary enrollment at the point reported.
caveat: The report covers early postsecondary outcomes; longer-term completion and labor-market reports are still pending.

title: When Schools Stay Open Late: The National Evaluation of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Program New Findings
authors: Mark Dynarski, Susanne James-Burdumy, Mary Moore, and colleagues
finding: The federal evaluation's follow-on findings report separates outcomes for the randomized elementary sample and the matched middle-school sample, including safety and behavior measures.
caveat: It is a companion analysis of the same national evaluation period, so it adds outcome detail rather than an independent program replication.

title: Addressing Chronic Absenteeism in Schools: A Meta-Analysis of Evidence-Based Interventions
authors: Katie Eklund, Matthew K. Burns, and Kari A. Oyen
finding: The meta-analysis synthesizes school-based interventions intended to improve attendance and identifies variation by intervention type and study design.
caveat: The reviewed interventions differ substantially in population, implementation, and attendance measure, so the synthesis is not a single program effect.

title: Multiple Inference and Gender Differences in the Effects of Early Intervention: A Reevaluation of the Abecedarian, Perry Preschool, and Early Training Projects
finding: A reanalysis of landmark randomized early-childhood programs assesses outcome families jointly and finds support for lasting benefits in several domains.
caveat: The programs were unusually intensive, small, and historically specific; results do not establish effects for typical contemporary preschool.

title: Effects of the Tennessee Prekindergarten Program on Children's Achievement and Behavior Through Third Grade
authors: Mark W. Lipsey, Dale C. Farran, and Kelley Durkin
finding: Follow-up of Tennessee's randomized pre-K evaluation reported that early advantages did not persist on the measured later achievement outcomes and documented concerning later behavioral patterns.
caveat: The results concern Tennessee's program and comparison conditions during the study period, not every public pre-K model.

title: Success Outcomes of Full-Day Kindergarten: More Positive Behavior and Increased Achievement in the Years After
authors: John R. Cryan, Robert Sheehan, and Jane Wiechel
finding: The study compares full-day and half-day kindergarten participation on later achievement and behavior outcomes.
caveat: This is an older nonrandomized comparison, so selection and local program design limit causal interpretation.

title: AI Literacy in K-12: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Lorena Casal Otero, Alejandro Catala, and Carmen Fernandez-Morante
finding: The review maps K-12 AI-literacy research and implementation approaches, highlighting that the field is newer than the established tutoring evidence base.
caveat: It reviews AI literacy rather than proving that generative-AI tutoring improves student learning outcomes.

title: Effects of Dual-Language Immersion Programs on Student Achievement
authors: Jennifer Steele, Robert Slater, and Gema Zamarro
finding: Lottery-based evidence estimates the effects of access to dual-language immersion programs on student achievement.
caveat: Results depend on the language model, school context, applicant group, and time spent in the program.

title: The Impact of Induction and Mentoring Programs for Beginning Teachers: A Critical Review of the Research
authors: Richard M. Ingersoll and Michael Strong
finding: The review finds that induction and mentoring evidence is generally favorable for teacher commitment and practice, while effects vary by program design and outcome.
caveat: It synthesizes heterogeneous programs and includes studies with different comparison designs, so it is not an estimate for one comprehensive induction model.

title: Free Lunch for All! The Effect of the Community Eligibility Provision on Academic Outcomes
authors: John Gordanier, Orgul D. Ozturk, and Breyon Williams
finding: The study estimates academic-outcome changes associated with schools adopting the Community Eligibility Provision.
caveat: Adoption is not random, and results depend on the policy setting, eligible schools, and outcome measure.

title: Reengaging High School Dropouts: Early Results of the National Guard Youth ChalleNGe Program Evaluation
authors: Dan Bloom, Alissa Gardenhire-Crooks, and Conrad Mandsager
finding: Early randomized evaluation results document reengagement outcomes for participants in the residential National Guard Youth ChalleNGe program.
caveat: The early follow-up does not answer the same longer-run employment and earnings questions as later reports.

title: Core Knowledge Language Arts
finding: The What Works Clearinghouse intervention report reviews eligible research on Core Knowledge Language Arts and its literacy outcomes.
caveat: A clearinghouse review is limited to the studies meeting its screening rules and should not be read as an effect for every knowledge-rich curriculum.

title: The Effect of Teacher Coaching on Instruction and Achievement: A Meta-Analysis of the Causal Evidence
authors: Matthew A. Kraft, David Blazar, and Dylan Hogan
finding: The meta-analysis pools causal evaluations of teacher coaching and reports larger effects on instructional practice than on student achievement.
caveat: Average results mask variation in coaching dose, subject focus, coach expertise, and scale.

title: Does Teacher Preparation Matter? Evidence about Teacher Certification, Teach for America, and Teacher Effectiveness
authors: Linda Darling-Hammond, Deborah Holtzman, and Su Jin Gatlin
finding: The analysis compares teacher preparation pathways and reported student-achievement differences in the California context.
caveat: This is not a randomized comparison and has been debated; it is included as a contrasting pathway study, not a decisive estimate.

title: Continued Progress: Promising Evidence on Personalized Learning
authors: John F. Pane, Elizabeth D. Steiner, Matthew Baird, and Laura S. Hamilton
finding: RAND's follow-up report compares participating personalized-learning schools with matched comparison schools and describes implementation conditions alongside achievement findings.
caveat: The participating schools were early adopters and the study does not isolate one product, platform, or practice as the cause of observed differences.

title: College Preparatory Curriculum for All: Academic Consequences of Requiring Algebra and English I for Ninth Graders in Chicago
authors: Elaine Allensworth, Takako Nomi, Nicholas Montgomery, and Valerie E. Lee
finding: The peer-reviewed analysis examines Chicago's ninth-grade college-preparatory requirement, including course performance and academic consequences.
caveat: The district policy changed several elements at once and does not establish the effect of Algebra I alone in every setting.

title: The Postsecondary Achievement of Participants in Dual Enrollment: An Analysis of Student Outcomes in Two States
authors: Melinda Mechur Karp, Juan Carlos Calcagno, and Katherine L. Hughes
finding: The study compares postsecondary outcomes for dual-enrollment participants and similar nonparticipants in two states.
caveat: Participation is not randomly assigned, and the estimate is sensitive to the comparison construction and state policy context.

title: The Impressive Effects of Tutoring on PreK-12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
authors: Andre Nickow, Philip Oreopoulos, and Vincent Quan
finding: The experimental tutoring synthesis provides comparative evidence relevant to both in-person and technology-supported high-dosage tutoring models.
caveat: The review does not isolate the effects of one branded tutoring provider or software platform.

title: The Impact of Enhancing Students' Social and Emotional Learning: A Meta-Analysis of School-Based Universal Interventions
finding: The meta-analysis synthesizes universal school-based SEL interventions across social-emotional, behavioral, and academic outcomes.
caveat: Interventions vary in curriculum, delivery quality, and measurement, so average effects do not identify one required SEL model.

title: A Review of Research on Project-Based Learning
finding: The review assesses the then-available research on project-based learning, including achievement and implementation questions.
caveat: The underlying studies are heterogeneous and many predate current standards, assessments, and digital tools.

title: The Causal Effects of Cultural Relevance: Evidence from an Ethnic Studies Curriculum
authors: Thomas S. Dee and Emily K. Penner
finding: The published analysis estimates effects of San Francisco's ethnic-studies assignment rule for students near the eligibility cutoff.
caveat: The design is most informative at the cutoff and for the district's particular curriculum and implementation.

title: The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Study: Early Impact and Implementation Findings
authors: James J. Kemple, William Corrin, Elizabeth Nelson, and colleagues
finding: The early report describes implementation and first-year impacts for the randomized supplemental literacy-course evaluation.
caveat: It is an earlier follow-up from the same research program and does not answer longer-term persistence questions.

title: Making Progress Toward Graduation: Evidence from the Talent Development High School Model
authors: James J. Kemple, Corinne Herlihy, and Thomas E. Smith
finding: The evaluation compares outcomes in Talent Development high schools and comparison schools during implementation of the restructuring model.
caveat: The comparison design and bundled school changes make it difficult to isolate individual model components.

title: National Early Literacy Panel: Developing Early Literacy
finding: The panel synthesizes evidence on early literacy skills and instructional practices that predict later conventional literacy.
caveat: It is a synthesis of early-literacy research, not a new evaluation of the National Reading Panel itself.

title: Community Schools as an Effective School Improvement Strategy: A Review of the Evidence
finding: The evidence review synthesizes evaluations of integrated student supports and community-school strategies.
caveat: Community schools are multi-component models, and the review does not identify a single universally effective service bundle.

title: The Effects of Teacher Evaluation on Teacher Performance
authors: Thomas S. Dee and James Wyckoff
finding: The study evaluates changes in teacher performance associated with a high-stakes teacher evaluation system in Washington, DC.
caveat: It estimates effects in one district's system and cannot separate every component of feedback, observation, dismissal, and incentives.

title: Project Follow Through
finding: The program archive documents the history, models, and published results associated with the federal Project Follow Through initiative.
caveat: This is a program-hosted historical resource and should be read alongside independent analyses of the original evaluation.

title: The Harlem Children's Zone: Promise Neighborhoods and the Neighborhood Effects Debate
authors: Roland G. Fryer Jr. and Will Dobbie
finding: The study analyzes student achievement in Harlem Children's Zone schools and considers the role of the school model and neighborhood services.
caveat: The design cannot cleanly separate school effects from selection, location, and the surrounding support network.

title: Student Achievement in Public Magnet, Public Comprehensive, and Private City High Schools
finding: The study compares achievement patterns across magnet, comprehensive public, and private urban high schools.
caveat: School enrollment is selective, so observed differences do not establish the causal effect of magnet-school attendance.

title: Principal Pipelines: A Feasible, Affordable, and Effective Way for Districts to Improve Schools
finding: The report evaluates district principal-pipeline systems using matched comparison schools and implementation evidence.
caveat: The package combines multiple leadership investments and cannot isolate one hiring, preparation, or support component.

title: Learning from Summer: Effects of Voluntary Summer Learning Programs on Low-Income Urban Youth
finding: The randomized study reports effects of voluntary district summer-learning programs and relates outcomes to attendance and instructional conditions.
caveat: Effects depend on participation and local program quality; a voluntary summer offer is not equivalent to mandatory extended schooling.
